utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. After a non-sitting week, we'll resume which case, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to deal briefly with a few matters -- no, perhaps I leave them. None of them are really urgent. We leave them until after we've heard the testimony of the first witness, the first witness who will appear before this Court through videolink. Mr. Stojanovic -- Madam Registrar, is the videolink functioning properly?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's confirmed to me that videolink is functioning properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's establish whether the -- at this moment I can see the representative of the Registry seated next to what I expect to be today's witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you confirm that you can hear us and that you can see us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, yes. We have the connection running.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can you see us? Can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is some noise, a buzzing noise. It's not perfect. I have this buzzing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way to resolve that? Is it a local problem on the other side of the videolink?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we would need a couple of minutes to finish the tests. We didn't have time to finish them. With your permission, could we please take five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll take a short break of five minutes so that the audio is also functioning well without any disturbance. The Chamber would like to be informed once the tests have been done. We take a break of most likely not more than five minutes. --- Break taken at 9.43 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber understands that the technical problems have been resolved. Let's give it another try. Could we seek, first of all, confirmation from the other side of the videolink that both video and audio are working well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, thank you. The connection has improved and we can continue. I apologise for the delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could we hear from the representative of the Registry who else are present in the room -- in the videolink room?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, this is me, Anna Vertelinkova, representative of the Registry. The witness is with me and a member of the ITSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you so much for that. Then, Witness, I take it that you're Mr. Gagovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you. If it doesn't cause you any physical problems, could I invite you to stand and make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gagovic. Please be seated. Mr. Gagovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Gagovic.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to give us your full name, slowly, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Miladin Gagovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagovic, have you given a statement, a written statement, to the Defence team of General Mladic in response to the questions put to you by the investigators?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask that we have document 65 ter 1D01670 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagovic, in front of you, I suppose you can see the statement that we also can see here in the courtroom. I'm asking you if the signature on the cover page of the statement is yours and if the information contained on this page is accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We also can see it here in front of us in e-court. Is this also your signature and is this the date written on the statement written by your hand?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before we continue, the Chamber does not have the document on its screen in e-court. There we are. Yes. It has been fixed. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagovic, during proofing for your testimony, you indicated that there were two typos in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at paragraph 4, and I would like the court services to zoom in on paragraph 4 in the witness statements in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the word "evezelje [phoen]" should be -- or, rather, "vozulja" should be eliminated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This should be moved away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You also told me that in paragraph 14 of your statement, please pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And also in e-court can we zoom in on paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The toponym "Kace" is mentioned, and you told me that the name of that geographic location is Kacelj, so LJ should be added to the end of that word; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now that we have made those two corrections for the record, I would like to ask you whether if I were to ask you the same questions today would you adhere to your statement including the two corrections that we have made? Did you provide your statement to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this statement represent the true account of what you know about the events that you testify about?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender Miladin Gagovic's statement into evidence. At the moment, it is 65 ter 1D01670.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we do so, Witness, would you give the same answers as far as the substance is concerned -- no, I think you've answered that question already. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jeremy. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1670 receives number D682, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D682 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to read a summary of Miladin Gagovic's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Miladin Gagovic is an All People's Defence teacher by profession. Before the war broke out, he was appointed as the commander of a company in the part of the town known as Dugo Polje by the Crisis Staff in Foca. Donja Polje. He had 80 men under him in his unit. The conflict in Foca broke out in April 1992. The fighting lasted some ten days. The Serb established power in Foca and the units which had participated in the fighting were organised according to the principle of Territorial Defence. The VRS did not exist in Foca at the time. The command chain went via the Crisis Staff up to June 1992, when the 1st Foca Brigade was established in Previla. That unit became an element of the Foca tactical group, headed and commanded by Marko Kovac. He was -- the witness was the company commander in this unit up to 14 September 1992, when he was wounded and referred for treatment. From December 1992, he was the assistant for logistics in the battalion, and then from 1994 he was in charge of personnel affairs in the Foca Brigade. He will testify about the fact that the Muslim population started leaving Foca even before the conflict started. They went wherever they could and most of them left towards Gorazde, particularly after the fighting started in the town of Foca. Finally, the witness speaks about the front line which was set up facing Gorazde and claims that in late May 1992 they did not send reports to the superior command and that the communications with the command went by courier. His unit never received either an oral or written order to act against Muslim civilians to expel them or to do anything illegal in their actions. This was a short summary of this witness's statement, and with your leave, Your Honours, I would have just a couple of questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagovic, in your statement in paragraph 9, you mention the establishment of a tactical group, the establish of the 1st Foca Brigade. You were appointed a company commander at that time. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber when that happened and where?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Foca Brigade was established in the Previla sector in late June, on the 27th or 28th of June. That's when I was appointed a company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say in the Previla sector, could you please tell the Trial Chamber where the Previla sector is?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Previla is in the territory of the Foca municipality, some 25 kilometres away from Foca in the direction of Jabuka commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Up to then, up to that date, i.e. the 28th of June 1992, was there an organised military structure in Foca as part of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before that date as the company commander in Donje Polje, who did you receive your direct orders from?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I received my orders from the Crisis Staff of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would kindly ask you in light of paragraph 12 of your statement to tell us what happened when you returned to your unit after the treatment? That was in 1993, 1994 -- 1994. Where was the command of the Foca Brigade then? Where were you physically located?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The command was in the Foca sector in a place known as Velecevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please give us some more details about the facility. What was it used for before the war?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The facility was a prison before the war. As far as I remember, it was for women only. That's where the brigade command was located during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What were your specific tasks as the officer in charge of personnel affairs in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: My duty was to be in charge of personnel affairs, to set up units, to send people for treatment, to replace them with other people. Those were my regular duties. I also sent reports on the strength of the unit and their presence in various parts of the battle-field.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Gagovic, you said that Muslims started leaving Foca even before the conflict broke out and especially after the conflict broke out and during the skirmishes in the town of Foca. How do you know that? How do you know that Muslims started leaving even before the war?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I stand by my statement. I lived in Foca before the war started. My next door neighbours were Muslims. They left and they -- as they were leaving they asked me, What are you waiting for? Why did you not leave already? After they left, I sent my family to Montenegro as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What about the other inhabitants of Foca, those of Serb ethnicity? Did they act in the same way as you? Did they also send their families away from the combat zone?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I believe so. A lot of people left Donje Polje because Donje Polje was where the most Muslims resided in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gagovic. I have no further questions for you at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for the time given to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. I have one very simple question, a line which I just do not understand. It may be a translation issue. Paragraph 14, the first sentence reads: "The line Borovac-Hrinci," et cetera, "was established as a separation and defence line." Then the second sentence reads: "In late may 1992, the line Osanica," et cetera, "was established." And the third sentence reads, "One they we withdrew." "Day" being spelled as t-h-e-y. I've got no idea whether there is any mistake. Whether the witness could tell us again what the third sentence means which apparently in the original starts with "jedan dan." Witness, could you tell us what that short sentence, starting with the word "jedan" means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One day we were attacked on the line Borovac-Hrncici-Gorca voda by Muslim forces from the direction of Gorazde. We suffered losses, we had dead and wounded, and we withdrew to another line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a technical problem Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have not received interpretation from the moment the witness started speaking. Neither the General nor I received any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean started speaking in the response to my question or during the last ten minutes entirely?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We heard you, we heard the interpretation of your words, but we did not hear the witness's answer in B/C/S. There was no sound coming from that side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'll briefly read what was translated to us because it goes well beyond my question, as a matter of fact. The witness, and he should carefully listen whether it reflects his words, said: "One day we were attacked on the line Borovac-Hrncici-Gorca voda by the Muslim forces from the direction of Gorazde. We suffered losses, we had dead and wounded, and we withdrew to another line." And what I also heard but which seems not to appear -- no, I think "one day" is the clue to the answer. And, Mr. Stojanovic, I asked just to explain the day and I now gained the impression, but you are better able to verify that, this where "day" is spelled at t-h-e-y, that it should have been spelled as d-a-y, so "one day we withdrew."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the witness has now confirmed this. This being clarified, Mr. Jeremy, are you ready to start your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll first tell the witness by whom he'll be cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, before that, I would say that on the basis of the -- the statement and on the basis of the direct testimony that I've heard today, I don't have any cross-examination. I made a time estimate on the basis that the videolink motion filed on the 7th of August, 2014, suggested that this witness would have unique evidence on the functioning and organisation of units in Foca, particularly of the tactical group and its relationship towards the Crisis Staff, VRS, and General Mladic. On that basis, I reserved some time for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: But I've not heard that evidence, so I don't have any cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jeremy. I would have a few questions, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your statement, you tell us that you were a company commander and that you were appointed as such verbally --

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Verbally, and I'm referring to paragraph 5 of your statement. Now in paragraph 6 of your statement you are referring to the month of April where armed fighting in Foca related to the take-over of power and control lasted about ten days. Were you in any way as a company commander involved in that fighting, or were those subordinate to you involved in that fighting?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: No. I provided security for the hospital. You will find it in paragraph 4 in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that happened in the month of April as well.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now in paragraph 9 of your statement, and I read it, it says: "It was announced that the Crisis Staff was established, that a tactical group was formed, somewhere in June 1992. And the 1st Foca Brigade was formed at Previla when I was a company commander." The first part of this sentence, "it was announced that the Crisis Staff was established," was that also in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I have some difficulties in reconciling that you performed your duty as a company commander in April, appointed by the Crisis Staff, if the Crisis Staff was established only in June 1992. Do you have an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff had existed when the conflict broke out in the territory of the municipality, and it was the Crisis Staff that appointed me as the company commander until June 1992. And then in June 1992 when the 1st Brigade was set up, I was also appointed as a company commander until the moment when I was wounded on the 14th of September, 1992, in Previla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the Crisis Staff existed already in June 1992 when the 1st Foca Brigade was formed because it was operational already in April. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, perhaps it's the language of the statement which confused me, the sequence of events. The matter is clear to me now. Have the questions by the Bench, Mr. Stojanovic, triggered any need for further questions? And I should ask you the same, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Mr. Gagovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. It was pretty short. At the same time, you should well understand that the evidence you've given is mainly to be found for this Chamber in the statement which was admitted into evidence and which is a statement of several pages. I would like to thank you very much for coming to the videolink room and for having answered questions that you were put to you by one of the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can conclude the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, is your next witness ready after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, although we were supposed to check during the break whether he has arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'll use the remaining time for a few matters. The first is that the Prosecution has advised the Chamber that it has received the B/C/S translation for P6748, which is 65 ter 31236, which was MFI'd through Witness Mihajlo Vujasin on the 16th of September, 2014, pending translation. This is all to be found on transcript page 25650. The translation has be received and is uploaded into e-court under doc ID M000-8567-BCST. If there are no objections from the Defence, the Chamber will instruct the Court Officer to attach the translation and that P6748 is now admitted into evidence. If there are any problems, Mr. Stojanovic, within 48 hours you can revisit the matter if there is any need to do that. Then I'd briefly deal with the documents which were MFI'd during the testimony of Nenad Kecmanovic. During the testimony of Nenad Kecmanovic, two documents were marked for identification: P6660, an excerpt from the transcript from the 114th Session of the BiH Presidency; and D557, the Islamic declaration by Alija Izetbegovic. Through an informal communication, the Chamber was informed that the parties have agreed on a selection to tender under P6660 but that a translation remains outstanding. Any update as far as the translation is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and good morning. We received that just last week and have provided it to the Defence and are just waiting for them to confirm that it's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'd like to hear soon from you, Mr. Stojanovic, in relation to the excerpt and its translation of P6660 so that the then reduced version can be uploaded. As regards D557, the Chamber was informed that the Defence wanted to tender the entire 77-page document, even though only a small number of pages was discussed with the witness. The Chamber would like to receive the reasons for tendering the entire document and requests the Defence to make submissions by the 20th of October of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We understand, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then finally another matter in relation to the notebooks of Witness Indjic. The parties have received copies of the notes handed over by Witness Indjic. The Chamber indicated on the 16th of September, 2014, at transcript page 25574 and -75 that it would await any submissions from the parties thereon. The Chamber now sets the dead-line of the 27th of October, 2014, for these submissions. And now there is another matter. Since we had a late start anyhow, I'll deal with the last item which is on my agenda, but we have to move into private session for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber is informed that the next witness will arrive by 11.00. We therefore take a break and we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. You're on your feet, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While the witness is entering, but before he starts, I would kindly ask for another half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we need one hour with this witness. He was sick the first time -- the first day he came late and I couldn't figure out properly how much time do we need before this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll see how your examination-in-chief develops and until this moment we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I want to go through this witness with the statement of one of the Prosecutor's Witness, RM081.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that's why we'll need more time. And we'll probably have to go into private session for that all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'll say one thing about that. It's usually not that we go through the statement of another person with a witness, you ask him questions about the same matter, and if there is any inconsistency or any contradiction then, of course, you put to the witness what another witness may have said. Just in order to have an orderly examination. Apologies, Mr. Jankovic, I take it, for not welcoming you when entering the courtroom and to continue our discussions we had. Apologies for that. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, you will first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would kindly ask the assistance from the usher just for a second to give Mr. Jankovic clean statement. Can you check with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In front of you you have a statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, whatever this witness may have in front of him, it's a good tradition that we first establish his identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] I'm trying to establish that, the numbers. We speeded up a bit this morning, so I don't have the number of this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it refresh your memory, Mr., if -- let me see. I do not see even the translation. Would it be 1D01696a, signed witness statement of Jankovic, Milenko, which you would like to have on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now you could ask the witness for his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were not here, Your Honour, I was very cautious. Now I'm pretty relaxed because I know I'm under good control. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm already the second who reminded you of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please state your full name slowly for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Milenko Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, have you given a statement to the Defence team of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the screen before you, can you see the cover page of the statement and the signature? Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it and that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, I already asked you to make a pause after my question because it needs to be translated into English, so wait for a few seconds before you start your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have the last page of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, in front of you, you can see the last page of the statement. Do you recognise the signature on it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are now going to make a correction that you drew my attention to last night, specifically in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have paragraph 5 of your statement on the screen. That's page 2 in the B/C/S and page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, it says here that you joined the Rogatica Company in May of 1992 and that at the time you assumed the duty of the Rogatica company commander. Is that correct or should it be amended?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It should be corrected because I did not have very clear recollection of all the dates at the time when I gave my statement, so therefore later on after reading certain documents, I came across information that it took place on the 25th of July, 1992, following the death of my relative who was the company commander of the Rogatica Brigade at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: His name was Milos Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What took place, then? Was it the formation of the company or the appointment of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Appointment of the witness the day after the killing of the previous commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When was Milos Jankovic killed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Milos Jankovic was killed on the 24th of May --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May or July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. No, I'm sorry. July. I am a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us what documents you read which made you aware of the date not being the correct date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents that I read are the following: I had a list of the combatants who got killed in the area of Rogatica municipality from the outbreak of war until the end of war, and that refreshed my memory concerning the date when I actually took over this position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you brought these documents with you to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these documents are in my hotel room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record I would just read how first three sentences of the statement, paragraph 5, should read now after this correction. I quote: "This lasted two or three months. Then a unit was formed, the Rogatica Company, sometime in May 1992. I joined the company at about this time and took up the duty of the commander of the Rogatica Company on 25th July, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just a clarification for me. The first sentence reads in the original statement: "This lasted two to three months."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now you read: "This lasted two or three months."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I misread, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay, then the original stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The original stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, this morning the OTP asked me something which I would like to clarify with you. In paragraph 3 of your statement, it reads that one such unit was formed in Pjesevica village. [In English] P-j-e-s-e-v-i-c-a. Only P-j-e-c-e, no s, c-e.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: If I may be of any help.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So is this the correctly spelled name of the village?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it should read P-l-j-e-s-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Plj, Plj. Yes. So P-l-j-e-s-e-v-i-c-a, a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We quickly move on now because the last spelling on the transcript seems to be the correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on quickly before we have another version. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After these corrections had been made, Mr. Jankovic, is the information you provided in your statement truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: All the information contained in the statement are truthful and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, would you provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I would completely give the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would move and offer this statement into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1696a receives number D683, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Now the transcript started reading that Mr. Jeremy was expressing there were no objections, then apparently this was removed but your words are not reflected at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, now you're Mr. Bos, but still not your own identity but you are relatively new, Mr. MacDonald, aren't you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Once again, Your Honours, no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are. It took Mr. Lukic three times to get the right thing on the transcript, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not only me this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- therefore it's one-to-one at this moment. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would just read the short summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. I take it that you have explained to the witness the purpose of doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And I did not have time to distribute this to the translators, but I will be reading slowly and it's very short.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The English booth doesn't have either version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Milenko Jankovic was born 20th of April, 1961, in Rogatica. Witness will testify of arming of Serbs in Rogatica, their self-organisation in villages in Rogatica municipality. He will explain his knowledge on forming of Rogatica Brigade, its organisation, strength, and activities in its zone of replenishment. He will testify on Muslim attacks in Rogatica municipality in 1992, particularly from the direction of Kozici, bordering with area controlled by Muslims. He will testify on clashes which occurred in June 1992 when city of Rogatica was partially put under control of Serb forces. He will explain circumstances of Muslim population leaving Rogatica. Upon Rogatica Brigade was established, witness was company commander in the same. He will testify on reporting and relation with other parts of VRS. He will also testify on incidents from indictment related to Rogatica municipality, like about his knowledge about Rasadnik and Veljko Vlahovic school. And that was the end of this short summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. One very short question about the summary: Where in the statement does it say that Serbs were armed in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read there that trusted people were armed. Is that to understand that only Serbs were trusted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Arms were only given to trusted people."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But among others things Serbs as well, among other people, or we can clarify with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I immediately put that to the witness. In your statement, Witness, where you say that only trusted people were given arms when arming was organised by the Territorial Defence. Could you tell us whether trusted people were to be found among all ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to explain. Those were the people who did not drink, who had no criminal past, who were not aggressive, or displayed any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was talking about ethnicity. Were any arms issued to non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say this exactly. I think that was the case because in my unit I also had Muslim members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they armed by the Territorial Defence at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, very briefly, who was at the head of the Territorial Defence and what was his ethnicity? And I'm talking about Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Serbian Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, the joint TO.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: At the head of the joint TO was Meho Agic or Mehmed Agic. I think that was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Meho Agic was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you also clarify the apparent existence of two TOs, the Serb TO and a joint TO, and which TO then was distributing weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, you heard the Judge's question. Can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Following the division of the municipality into two parts, the Serbian municipality and the Muslim municipality, automatically there was a division in the police force and Territorial Defence. The Serbian Territorial Defence armed the Serbian population, including a number of Muslims who were attached to the Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness also tell us up until what point in time there was the joint TO and when the TO, the Serb TO, was established?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, you heard the question. I'm sure that you have problems with the dates, but can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you an exact date, but I do know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are supposed not to tell the witness already in advance that he may have problems. He will tell us and there should be no suggestion --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of that kind. Yeah. Okay. Then he will tell us. It should not be part of the question. Not an exact date. But you said you do know what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know the municipal assembly of Rogatica made the unanimous decision on dividing Rogatica municipality into two municipalities. I really can't remember the date of that meeting, but according to that decision the administration, the police, the Territorial Defence, everything was divided into the Serb municipality on the one side and the Muslim municipality on the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you remember the month that this happened, if you don't remember the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's difficult for me to remember the month when that happened. I know that it was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether it was in the month of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you don't know exactly. Let's not speculate, then. You mentioned earlier today that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, nevertheless, I'm still confused. Considerably confused. Witness, I asked you to explain what were the people trusted sufficiently to receive weapons. You said they were those who were not drinking but also Muslims would receive weapons. I asked you in relation to paragraph 4 of your statement, that Muslims were -- whether Muslims were provided as well, I asked were any arms issued to non-Serbs. Your answer was: "I cannot say this exactly. I think that was the case because in my unit I also had Muslim members." I asked were they armed by the Territorial Defence at this moment, and you said yes. Was that at that point in time the Serb Territorial Defence which was providing arms to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they given directly to the Muslims or were they given to you as a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not directly to Muslims. They were given to people who at the time were the organisers of village guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And village guards therefore were of mixed ethnicity? Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were villages where those guards were of mixed ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in your unit, as you called it, who were the Muslims that received weapons through these channels? Could you give us names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were two brothers, Ezo and Himzo Golic who received them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us about your unit. What about Muslim members in other units who received weapons to those celubs [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for example in Stojan Petkovic's unit there were also two brothers who were Muslims. I can't remember their names but their family name was Drago. They were from the village of Socica, the hamlet of Draguljevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I'm going to ask you. We'll try not to go into private session because after my question I'm just going to cite the paragraph number of the statement of a protected witness, RM081.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the guidance I got from Judge Orie where you want to see the statement on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's -- you first have to ask the witness about the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the facts are facts which are subject of any statements by any other witness, then you can put it to the witness after he has answered the questions, but of course the first question is has he read already those statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He has?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, did you receive any instructions, specific instructions when you were reading a statement? And we now move into private session before you answer that question. Madam Registrar, can we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct that I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. We first move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, did Serb policemen decide to walk out from the joint SUP? Did they do it of their own will or did that happen under some other circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, I mentioned that decision on the split of the municipality into the Muslim and Serbian municipalities, and I also emphasised that at the same time the Ministry of the Interior was split as well as the Territorial Defence. In other words, this was pursuant to a municipal decision on the division of the municipality into two parts. In other words, it was done on a decision not of an -- of anybody's own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there markings on the uniform of the Serb policemen depicting the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still, the decision, and I do not know whether the Prosecution would be in a position to agree with you on when that decision was taken, but we'd very much like to have a better time-frame in order to better evaluate the answers of this witness. So was it a written decision, was it an oral decision, is it documented, et cetera? That is all relevant factual information this Chamber would need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we heard our witness, Mr. Sokolac, and the document was introduced through his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then why not put to the witness whether it would refresh his recollection if -- and the date of that decision was, if the parties would agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- I really had problems with this witness with the dates, and I was trying to avoid --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm -- at this moment, I'm seeking whether the parties can agree on the date of that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] We'll have that decision shortly if -- my colleague will go out and bring the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well I -- the first thing I would like to have is a date. Prosecution, any suggestion as to the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, through the Defence witness, Mr. Sokolac, there was a report dated the 22 of June, 1992, which referred to the date of the division as the 2nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2nd of May. Is that also the Defence's position, that the 2nd of May was the date of the division?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, that is P6773.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And before you do so, Mr. Lukic, just to refer you to the question you asked at page 34, lines 24, it was a leading question: "Were there markings on the uniform of the Serb policemen depicting the SDS?" The correct question is: Were there any markings, if so, what were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, we heard the number of the document as well as the date. Do you know if in the building of the municipality there was an arms depot belonging to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I am an employee of the administrative services of the municipality of Rogatica, and I know only too well that that building does not even have a basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your conversations with others, did you hear that weapons were stored there at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I never heard that there were any weapons in the municipal building of Rogatica, that it was ever -- that they were ever stored in the building of the municipality of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that the military wanted to take something from the Territorial Defence in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. What?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that members of the then JNA arrived in front of the public security station building in Rogatica to take over the military files of JNA members from the then department of defence. I know that Mr. Ahagic was ready and willing to hand over that documentation. However, members of the Rogatica police station prevented that. An incident occurred. A member of the police in civilian clothes, whose family name was Alagic, tried to disarm a member of the then JNA, who was Albanian by ethnicity. I don't know his name. And then the soldier used his knife and hit the police member. No fire was open at the time. There was no exchange of fire of any sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think also reference as to, apparently, also the content of the statement of a protected witness should not be done in open session. You can do that later, ask for private session, say that this related to that, that related to this, but you already -- you already give some information about what a protected witness has said. And therefore, Madam Registrar, would you please make a redaction. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Shall I just ask then every time to go to private session just to quote? Because it will be too late to go -- if I go -- because I will have a lot of paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do not know whether -- do you want to put them to the witness or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can put it to the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- refer to what paragraph that statement is, then you ask for private session later on and say the testimony of this witness about A is linked in the Defence's view to paragraph so-and-so of the protected witness, you can make that a list, or even do it in writing and make a confidential submission but not do it the way in which you were doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then I would proceed along the same lines, and finally we will end up with a list. When we have the final version of the transcript, we will be able to pin-point the paragraph number. [In English] Let's go to the private session. I think it would be much faster and we should have then this statement on our screens but not to be broadcasted to the public. And I don't know if you have to put down the blinds behind the witness, because he has to have this statement on his screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would read the relevant portion of the statement to the witness, but then -- yes, we don't have any B/C/S version. Or summarise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's not too long --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- please read it. But only in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll take a break and we'll resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Stojanovic, the Chamber understood that it's your wish not to start the examination-in-chief of the next witness. Let us be very clear. You should be prepared. That's one. And whether we'll insist on the witness to come to this building, we'll see how the present witness, the examination of the present witness develops, and then we'll decide in accordance with that. But you should be prepared if any time is left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone was not activated, but I did understand, Mr. Stojanovic, that you have no problems with what I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We can stay in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, can you quickly tell us a few names of the ten first Serbian soldiers that were killed on the 19th of June, 1992? The ones that you can remember.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Those killed were Sava Losic; then last name Stjepanovic, I can't remember his first name; also killed was Miladin Losic; Tomo Rajak; Miroslav Jovicic; and some others whom I cannot remember at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was warned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did any of the Serbian units in Rogatica have flamethrowers?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, and I can guarantee for that because I have the knowledge that this kind of devices, flamethrowers, were removed from the JNA arsenal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had there ever been any activity by the Uzice Corps in the area of Rogatica or any part thereof?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can fully confirm that the Uzice Corps or any units belonging to it was operational in the area of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Was not operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's move now to Veljko Vlahovic school. Can you tell us who was accommodated there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The people who were accommodated in the Veljko Vlahovic school were both Muslim and civilians of other ethnicities. The purpose was to provide protection for them in the course of combat that was going on in the town of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you remember any names of non-Muslims who were accommodated there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: My uncle was in the school, secondary school, Veljko Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the name of his uncle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please repeat the name of your uncle who was at the Vlahovic school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His name was Milorad Neskovic and his wife, Vera. There was also a relative of mine named Veljko Sucula. There was also Vlasta Gavric, she was a Croat woman married to a Serb. There were also the Brusin family, the whole family, daughter Silvja, sons, Zdenko and Boro. I don't remember the name of his wife. And there were other families as well whose names I cannot recall right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement you say that you never entered the secondary school. What's the source of your knowledge who were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true that I had never gone to the Veljko Vlahovic secondary school; however, I learned about this from the soldiers who were securing the facility about who was accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, what's the purpose of securing a facility if they are just there for their own well-being?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose was as follows: The facility was security solely in order to prevent anyone coming to it because everybody was armed at the time and preventing any incidents from happening. There were families who lost their members and in order to prevent any form of retaliation that is why there was personnel on duty inside the facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And was that the result, that everyone could leave sound and safe that facility being -- having been protected there by these guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] People are free to go wherever they wanted. However, it was suggested for the benefit of their personal safety not to leave the facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. My question was whether everyone who had been protected there survived well having enjoyed this protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so. I have no information that anyone was killed in the facility. I don't think that ever happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And no one was taken by anyone else from that facility and did not survive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The ground around the Veljko Vlahovic school, was it mined in that period, June, July, August, September, and further on of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can say with 100 per cent certainty that there were no minefield around this facility. How do you plant mines around a school in town? It's inconceivable. And I can claim that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the food was being prepared for the people who stayed at the Veljko Vlahovic school?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The meals were prepared for those people at Upi Trans, and it was delivered at the same time as it was delivered to members of the Rogatica Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say at the same time. Was it the same food or was it different?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Totally identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How do you know that? What kind of connection do you have with Upi Trans?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the headquarters of the 1st Rogatica Company was at Upi Trans and that is where the kitchen was which provided meals for members of the Territorial Defence as well as for the people who were at the secondary school Veljko Vlahovic in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there any water-supply in the school or was there a shortage of water?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: There was water throughout the whole period because waterworks were operational. There were sanitation and other equipment in the school. The school had some ground floor rooms where windows were facing east, whereas there were no windows on the west side of the school. And there were two flats inside the facility occupied by a caretaker and one of the teachers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the fighting in Rogatica, did you see any burnt bodies scattered around Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I never saw a charred body in my life in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Following the combat operations, did you see a lot of decomposing bodies in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't because it's simply impossible. Decomposing bodies are a source of infectious disease; therefore, all the bodies should have been buried and as I say I never saw any of them on the streets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you limit yourself to what you saw and whether it would be possible or not on what should have been done is a totally different matter. If there is any question in relation to that, Mr. Lukic will ask you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Teocak is near Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you able to see that area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: From the Upi Trans facility where the company was stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see fires burning at Teocak where people were burnt or did you see any fires at all that were burning for a long time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not notice anything at Teocak and that same thing applies to the soldiers who were securing Upi Trans. Had that been the case, they would have been obliged to report such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now briefly about buildings, religious buildings. There were mosques in Rogatica. One of them was destroyed. Do you know when was the first one destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The first one was destroyed on the 24th of July, 1992. I'm sorry, 24th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this part of Rogatica under Serb control when this mosque was demolished?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbian forces were not in control of that part of the town where the mosque was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have other religious buildings been destroyed in Rogatica such as the synagogue or the Catholic church? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Muslim forces -- or members of Muslim units, rather, burned the synagogue, but the Catholic church remained intact because it was located in the Serbian part of the town of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know who destroyed the mosque on the 24th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. But I know that TO members in Rogatica were not in that part of town at that time. I don't know who destroyed the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: How come you know that that was on the 24th of June? What else happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: You know how. On that day our APC made a contact with the other part of the Serb territory and passed through that part of the town. An anti-tank mine was planted near the mosque and Slavisa Milackovic, who was driving the APC, was killed on that occasion. A passenger in the APC was wounded on that occasion. All that happened by the debris of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I would like to move on to something else. Do you know Tomo Batinic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he wounded during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was wounded. I believe that that happened in November 1992 in the Socica sector, in late November of that year, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that, did he immediately get involved in the work? What happened to him after the wounding? What kind of a wound was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a serious bodily wound. Mr. Batinic lost an eye and he had serious injuries on his leg as well as lacerations on his face. He was referred for further treatment in Belgrade. He spent there over a year, and as far as I know he did not return. He did not occupy any other duties after he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Immediately after he was wounded, did he move around the town? Did he meet with people? Did he talk to people? Did he visit places around Rogatica? Was he able to do that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. He was seriously wounded. He lost an eye. His leg was injured. Therefore, he was not in a position to move around the town immediately after wounding. He was urgently transported to Belgrade and he stayed there for treatment for over a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us whether Mr. Batinic was a civilian, was he a military man? Was he -- what position did he have, if any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time Tomislav Batinic was the president of the assembly. He was a civilian. He was not a soldier. He was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just one more piece of information, if you know. How was he wounded?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic was in a vehicle and that vehicle hit a tank mine. He was returning from a field mission. The driver of the vehicle was killed and Tomo was wounded in the way I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you participated in the events in and around Rogatica, did you ever see a plan according to which one-third of Muslims from Rogatica had to be killed, one-third baptised and convert to do Christianity, and the last third should leave?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I claim with full support that I never heard from anybody, and especially not from my superiors, that something of that kind was planned to happen in the town of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just one more seemingly unimportant piece of information: Did you know Mirko Planojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he have a brother?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: He did have a brother. His name was Ozren Planojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, this is all that our Defence has prepared for you and we thank you for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Before we give an opportunity to the Prosecution to cross-examine you, Judge Fluegge would have one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just briefly. Witness, you told us about the destruction of the synagogue. Where have you been when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in the part controlled by the Serbian army or, rather, the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How far away from the synagogue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some 1500 metres, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you see the destruction with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How do you know that this was done by Muslim units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know because that part was under the control of Muslim units exclusively. Two Serbian cafes were torched at the same time as the synagogue and some private Serbian houses as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is a conclusion you have drawn from the location of the synagogue; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One other question. You told us about -- this can be found on page 47, lines 19 to 21: "I," talking about the school, "I learned about this from the soldiers who were securing the facility about who was accommodated there." What kind of soldiers were these? To which unit did they belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those soldiers were from the Territorial Defence, a company of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which Territorial Defence, the joint one or the Serbian one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serb Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I am, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. MacDonald. You'll find him to your right. Mr. MacDonald is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to move chronologically through events in 1992 as briefly as possible. Can you tell the Court when you first joined the Territorial Defence in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: 20th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 4 of your statement in relation to the distribution of weapons by the Territorial Defence, you state you were called when some of the weapons were received. Who exactly called you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So for the sake of clarity, this is the Serbian Territorial Defence that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You say you joined the 20th of April, 1992. When did this call take place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the date, but it was around that time when the Territorial Defence was first organised. That's when we were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court the type of weapons that you mention in paragraph 4 in relation to this arming?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Only small calibre infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: How many men were in the unit at the end of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I have to stress that I'm referring only to the village of Pljesevica where I lived and where defence was indeed organised. There were approximately some 50 or 60 people there but unarmed. Because small quantities of weapons were distributed, they were handed over to the village guards whose goal was to protect the population from a possible attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I believe you state that Milos Jankovic, your cousin, was the leader of the unit in Pljesevica. Who was his superior?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. The commander of the Territorial Defence was his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So far as you're aware, did your unit, the one in Pljesevica, ever receive any orders from Mehmet Adzic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: We never received any such order. Ever. I don't know. I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: For the sake of clarity, Witness, did that unit have any other goal other than protecting the village of Pljesevica at the time at the end of April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The only task that unit had was to protect the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder if at this point the Prosecution can have 65 ter number 31407, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: All right. Witness, what you see before you is an order from the 1st Romanija Brigade to the command of the Rogatica Brigade on 21st April 1992. It is a request for an assessment on the readiness of Territorial Defence units for combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can move to the second page in both. Your Honours, I have to apologise here. The English translation, unfortunately, did not contain the signature which Your Honours see on the B/C/S translation. I did bring that to the attention of those who translated it and I believe a revision is in process. When I move to tender this document, I will ask to MFI it, Your Honours, in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Please proceed for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I am obliged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
