utterances.text: Witness, who has signed this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It says Dragoljub Macar. I didn't know the man, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. If we can go back to the first page in both, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, it -- I appreciate I've said this already, Witness, but just to highlight the fact this is on the 21st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter number 31408. And, Your Honours, the second document is linked to the first document which is why I'm moving directly to it just now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, this is a report on the 30th of April, 1992. Do you see at the top just underneath to whom it is being sent that it states: "Pursuant to order dated 21st April, 1992, I hereby submit a report ..." Do you see that language?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot see it very well. Can this be zoomed in or something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, otherwise you'll read the relevant portion you want to draw the attention of the witness to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, Witness, this report does state it's being given pursuant to an order dated 21st April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can move to the last page in both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm right, Witness, in saying that it's been sent by the Territorial Defence commander Rasko Kusic on 30th April; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can see his name but there is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not "Rasko Kusic" but "Rajko Kusic." Just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I am obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we see on the -- let me see. Yes, I see that we are in paragraph 8 in the original, which is not visible in the English translation. But may I take it that we are looking at that because we see in capital letters, "We kindly request ...," which is part of paragraph 8 of this document. I'm just comparing the left --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honour is correct that the paragraph numbers are not reflected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can now please move to page 2 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S. My apologies, I have inverted those numbers. Page 3 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, near the top of the page we see the heading: "Pljesevica Company - Centre 2." Now, that's your unit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Pljesevica Company indeed was our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now just under it we see a -- well, we see the words "controlling the entrance into the city from the direction of Sarajevo towards Konanje and Zivaljevina and then securing," and there are a number of locations that follow. Is that in fact what your unit was doing on the 30th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know one part of the neighbourhood of Karanfil was joined to that unit unbeknownst to me. That unit that was in the territory of Pljesevica did not control the entrance to the city from the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can I just clarify the first sentence of your answer there. One part of the neighbourhood was joined to, I assume, your unit, but that was not known to you. Can you just explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I mean, the report. Maybe some other unit's competencies were reported as being part of the Pljesevica Company competency. I claim with full responsibility that we were not in that part of town and that we did not control the passage of vehicles on that road. Not towards the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: But you were deputy commander of this company, weren't you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can move on to the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Weaponry and possession. And it says "2 x 12.7mm PAM." What weapons are those, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's an anti-aircraft machine-gun, 12.7 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And did your unit in fact have two anti-aircraft guns, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct that two arrived in the unit but one was handed over to Donje Polje and one remained in the village of Pljesevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Witness, my understanding earlier was that your testimony was that you received light infantry weapons only. Are these light infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Those were not artillery weapons. An anti-aircraft machine-gun is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, don't change the question. The question is whether these were light infantry weapons. There was no suggestion that it was artillery or whatever. Are these light infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honours. I'll seek to tender both of those documents. Although pending the signature on the first one with the English translation, I'd ask that be MFI'd in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the first document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31407 receives number P6813.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And document 31408 receives number P6814, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. P6814 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If I can now move to May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: When the Rogatica Company was formed, how many men were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. Approximately a hundred men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Did the Pljesevica unit become this company or was it combined with others to become this company?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not the entire Pljesevica unit because most of that unit were elderly men who were unfit for service. They were just village guards. The newly set up company was composed of the population from militarily-able-bodied men from the part of town known as Karanfil.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Zoran Bojat?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Please repeat the name. I did not understand it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps it's my pronunciation. Perhaps I can spell it, the second name, B-o-j-a-t.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I know one from Pljesevica, the other from Borik. So I know two people by the same name, Zoran Bojat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31406.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This is a report by a Zoran Bojat to the Intervention Platoon Territorial Unit in Pljesevica and it is dated 19 May, 1992. Witness, in your statement you stated your company was an intervention one. Is this addressed to your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't read what it says here. Could you please read it for me? The picture is simply not clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Very well. In the top left-hand corner, it states, "Territorial Defence, Intervention Platoon, Pljesevica." The title is, "Report on reconnaissance of the area of Sjemec." I won't read the text, but it is a report submitted by Zoran Bojat. It is dated 19 May, 1992, from Borike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it possible to zoom in on the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps we can try and zoom in on the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Does that help, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Much easier. So I can read it, if you will allow me. Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait for a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps just now, Witness, if you just tell us whether this was addressed to your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Was there another Intervention Platoon in Pljesevica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is an Intervention Platoon that operated within the Borik battalion, and it was composed of people from Pljesevica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you now answer the question put to you by the Prosecutor, please. The question was are there more than one intervention platoons in the -- in this unit of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no Intervention Platoon at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: My apologies, Witness. Perhaps there was a mistranslation, which can clarify this. In your statement in paragraph 6, you state: "The company I led was an intervention company"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. That is the company that had been formed in Upi Trans, not in Pljesevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So it -- you're not aware which unit this report is being directed to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this report. I don't know who it is addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps I can take you to one part of it, nevertheless. The second sentence, Witness, states, "General mobilisation was carried out in the mentioned area ..." Were you aware of a general mobilisation taking place on 19 May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that there was general mobilisation. I do know, though, that people organised themselves and set up units in order to protect their villages and their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. You stated about self-organisation with regard to your own unit but that was under the command of Rajko Kusic; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if this might be a suitable point to have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a suitable time to have a break. Could you tell us how much more time you would need after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I would hope 30 minutes, Your Honours, but it may stretch to 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then there is no need to keep the next witness on standby. Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We would like to see you back after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are just to be ready that you're standing or is there anything that you would like to address, Mr. MacDonald?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: There is one matter that I would like to address, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just for Your Honours's information, I would not seek to tender the document that we were discussing just before the break, 31406.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, if I can remain with May 1992. You say in your statement other companies were formed in the Rogatica municipality, one in Kozici and one in Borike. Who was in command of the company in Kozici when it was formed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Spiro Pavlovski, I think was his name, was commander in Kozici. And in Borike that was a unit the size of a battalion - I made a mistake there - and it was under a direct command of the TO commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And you state that at some point a brigade was formed from all the units in Rogatica. What date did that take place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date. It is true that a brigade was formed after the TO became part of the Army of Republika Srpska, but I cannot remember the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald. You said the Borike unit, size of a battalion. It was under a direct command of the TO commander. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was Mr. Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I would now like to discuss a document from the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Before I request it be called up, the Rogatica Brigade was renamed to the Podrinje Brigade in late 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was called exactly the 1st Podrinje Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did the name change in late 1992; is that correct? That was also part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, I cannot remember at the moment. I don't think so. I think the name remained the same. Light brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour. Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter number 31402. If we can move to the second page of the document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this is a document dated 23rd November, 1994. It's been sent to the Drina Corps command from Rajko Kusic, who is identified as a commander of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade. It concerns an update to the list of officers in that brigade, and it will be referring back to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can please move to page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And, Witness, what I'm interested, and here are the columns along the top. I believe we see name, rank, date, place, and municipality of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we can scroll along to the right in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Almost in the middle of your page, a column that states "joined VRS on." Can you see those columns, Witness, or would you like the B/C/S made bigger?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, my sight is so bad. I can't find anything that you made reference to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps we can try and make it bigger, the column. Does that help you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see anything. Now I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And would you agree that it's a name, then rank, and then to the right of the page date, place, and municipality of birth?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is birth, identification number, date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we can scroll to the right in the document, please. Slightly further. Further to the right, sorry. If we keep scrolling. If that's -- yes, if we can hold it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The last full column on the right, Witness, am I right in saying the title of that is "Joined VRS on"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can go fully back to the left. And my thanks to the court assistants for scrolling back and forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The first name is Rajko Kusic. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can go back to the column "Joined VRS on."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And that states the 20th of May, 1992, doesn't it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we can once again scroll back to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If I can take you to the second name, one Milovan Lelek. Do you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And who is he, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That was the man whom I replaced on the 30th of November, 1993, at Borike, who had taken over the position of chief of staff of the Rogatica Brigade from Mile Vujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can scroll back to the column "Joined VRS on," please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And it states that he joined the VRS on 20th of May, 1992, as well; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can move to page 4 in the B/C/S and page 6 in the English, please. With Your Honours' leave, I would simply ask the B/C/S be put on the screen and we perform the same operation as we did for the initial two names. I'm looking for number 22, which is at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, number 22, is that your name that appears there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we scroll along to the right, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Under the column "Joined VRS ...," it says 20 May, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And, Witness, is this document accurate? Did you join the VRS on the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: According to the certificates that I provided from the draft office say that as of the 20th of April I was member of the TO Rogatica, and then as of 20th of May, 1992, I was a member of the Army Republika Srpska. Therefore, I think this is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If I can move on to the last chronological piece I intend to tackle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You state in paragraph 15 of your statement that Rajko Kusic was your immediate superior throughout the war. Until what date were you subordinated to Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Until the 30th of June, 1995 -- sorry, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Did you remain on the territory of Rogatica municipality throughout -- well, until 1996?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remained there in Rogatica until 1996 and further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, with thanks to my colleague, I would seek to tender the document 31402.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31402 receives number P6815, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, I'd now like to address a few statements you make in your statement. You state that there were two collection centres in Rogatica municipality, and that's at paragraph 12 of your statement. For the sake of clarity, do you accept there could have been more of these centres and that you were unaware of their existence?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that there were only two, only two centres. The Veljko Vlahovic secondary school and the Rogatica agricultural compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The second one that you refer to, is that more commonly known as Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It used to be an agricultural compound that was empty. It belonged to Agrokombinat and yes, its popular name was, indeed, Rasadnik. I suppose that it's because it used to be a nursery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour. Can the Prosecution please have P06774.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I am happy to read out the relevant parts to you, Witness. This is from Rajko Kusic on the 30th of November, 1992, to the municipal assembly of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: In the second paragraph in the English, Your Honours, about halfway down the page. It states -- sorry, in the middle of the first paragraph, Your Honours. My apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: "With your approval we have gathered civilians at the secondary school, church centre, and DP/socially owned enterprise/ Ergela in Rogatica. In accordance with the circumstances we were providing them with the same food as soldiers on the line had three times a day."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down while reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, this is your commander providing a report at the end of November 1992 and he is referring to other centres in Rogatica municipality. Do you accept there were other centres and you were unaware of their existence?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: If I may be allowed to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: A reference is made in here in this letter to the church centre in Rogatica. I was aware of it but it was only a reception centre. As far as I know, people didn't say there. They would be referred to the school immediately after just having been received there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have P02229 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness also explain Ergela or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Oh, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You told us about a church but what about the socially owned Ergela company, I take it, in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the company Agrokombinat in Rasadnik. I don't know where the term "Ergela" comes from. It used to be a cattle farm sometime in the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you consider it likely that it's actually the same but under a different name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, the document in front of you now is a report from the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior public security station in Rogatica, dated 17 June, 2004. I will read the relevant parts to you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: For Your Honours in the first paragraph just after the date 2nd of June, 2004, it states: "The information was gathered regarding collection centres where persons of Bosniak nationality stayed in the region of Rogatica."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, it then goes on to enumerate five such centres including the former nursery-garden, the building of the malt-house factory, the building of the high school, CJB Rogatica, and the building named the rectory. Now, Witness, if I can ask you again: Do you accept there were other collection centres in Rogatica other than the two that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps statements were taken from people when they arrived. I'm aware of the secondary school centre, I'm aware of this Rasadnik place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So, Witness, yes, you don't know about these other collection centres. That's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Very quickly with regards to the facility of Rasadnik. I'm right in saying you never observed the conditions, rather, in which detainees were held; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I entered the facility on several occasions, but I did not enter the area where people were kept. I just entered the office of the manager of this facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And with regard to the school, you've told us you're aware there were sanitation facilities there. But, Witness, you have no idea of the conditions in which detainees were held there either, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that there was always water during the war because the town was supplied from a source which was under the control of the Territorial Defence of Rogatica municipality. I really didn't enter those premises in order to see whether there was water or not, whether there were facilities working or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If I can move on, then. When you passed through Rogatica town, Witness, did you never see detainees performing forced labour such as chopping wood or cleaning up rubbish?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that detainees volunteered to work, to collect firewood, to work on private farms, because they would receive better food. They would even be given clothes and cigarettes. They volunteered for work. I never knew that they were forced to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'll move on from that topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask one question. You said that they would receive better food. Now you explained this before, that they got all this same food as all the soldiers got, three times a day. What was better than?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they worked in private households, if they sowed potatoes or something, in private homes food was better than from big cauldrons, and they also received cigarettes, and, yes, they normally received the same food as all of us. But in private homes, food was better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, where does this knowledge come from? How do you know exactly, for example, whether those detained in the Veljko Vlahovic school would voluntarily have reported for work? How do you know that? Of course, the Chamber has heard evidence about the situations in those institutions. At least, therefore, I'm wondering where your information comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those people came to my line and they prepared fuel wood there, and I know what they were saying, that they were much better off if they were out working in the field than if they stayed in the facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they worked close to or in any connection with the unit you were in at the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand your question. Could you please rephrase or repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said those people came to my line. May I take it that that is the front line or confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The defence line. The defence line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And they had to work close to the defence line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not have to do anything. They expressed a desire to work because nobody forced them to work, not on my line, and they never worked on the line itself. They worked in the depth of the territory, perhaps 200 metres or so away from the combat line -- I apologise, from the Defence line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, I see that it's time for -- to adjourn. And could you give us an indication as to how much more time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I think between probably around six or seven minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you give us an indication as to how much time you would need as matters stand now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am calculating, probably I will need six, seven minutes too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we are considering whether or not we could conclude the testimony of this witness which would then take another 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably 15 to 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fifteen to 20. Perhaps it's wiser to adjourn for the day. But then I take it that the parties will be very disciplined tomorrow and not think very early in the morning so therefore there are hours left. Witness, before we adjourn for the day I would like to instruct you that you should not speak to anyone or communicate in whatever other way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or whether that is testimony that you are still about to give tomorrow. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 14th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
